title: **Context:** B2B API middleware enabling banks and fintechs to issue and manage
description: **Context:** B2B API middleware enabling banks and fintechs to issue and manage virtual cards. Customers are bank/fintech product, engineering, operations, and compliance teams. End cardholders are two steps removed.

title: | ID | Source | Complaint | Segment | Frequency Reported | |----|--------|------
description:
| ID | Source | Complaint | Segment | Frequency Reported |
|----|--------|-----------|---------|---------------------|
| CMP-01 | Support ticket | Card creation API times out during bulk batch issuance (500+ cards), forcing manual retry logic on their end. | Digital Bank Engineering | 14 tickets / 60 days |
| CMP-02 | Account manager call | No webhook for card activation status. Team polls the status endpoint every 30 seconds, wasting API quota. | Fintech CTO | Recurring, 3 separate fintechs |
| CMP-03 | Support ticket | Card freeze action succeeds on the API but takes up to 4 minutes to reflect at the card scheme, causing failed transaction disputes from end customers. | Bank Operations | 9 tickets / 30 days |
| CMP-04 | Compliance escalation | No self-serve way to export card issuance/status logs by date range for CBN audit. Requires a support ticket and manual CSV pull by Interswitch staff. | Compliance Officer | Every audit cycle (quarterly) |
| CMP-05 | Sandbox feedback form | Sandbox environment resets test data unpredictably, breaking QA test suites the night before a release. | Fintech Engineering | 6 reports / 45 days |
| CMP-06 | Support ticket | Error codes returned on failed card creation are generic ("400 Bad Request") with no machine-readable reason, forcing manual log review by Interswitch support. | Digital Bank Engineering | 21 tickets / 90 days |
| CMP-07 | Renewal call | Limits and controls (spend cap, merchant category restriction) can only be set at card creation, not updated afterward without reissuing the card. | Bank Product Manager | Mentioned in 4 of 6 renewal calls |

title: **Note IN-02 — Fintech, Product Manager** > Our support team gets flooded with "
description:
**Note IN-02 — Fintech, Product Manager**
> Our support team gets flooded with "why is my card still not active" complaints. We can't tell the customer anything because we don't get pushed a status change — we only find out when we poll. By the time we poll, the customer has already called in.

title: **Note IN-03 — Bank, Operations Manager** > When fraud is suspected, every secon
description:
**Note IN-03 — Bank, Operations Manager**
> When fraud is suspected, every second matters. We call the freeze API, our dashboard shows "frozen," but the cardholder can still transact for a few minutes. We've had two disputes where the customer insists we didn't actually freeze it in time, and they're right.

title: **Note IN-04 — Fintech, Compliance Officer** > Every CBN audit cycle, I have to
description:
**Note IN-04 — Fintech, Compliance Officer**
> Every CBN audit cycle, I have to open a ticket, wait for Interswitch support to pull card logs manually, then reformat the CSV myself. It's the same request every quarter. I've started keeping my own shadow spreadsheet just so I'm not fully dependent on their turnaround time.

title: **Note IN-05 — Digital Bank, QA Engineer** > We can't trust sandbox test data to
description:
**Note IN-05 — Digital Bank, QA Engineer**
> We can't trust sandbox test data to persist between our nightly regression runs. Cards we created yesterday sometimes aren't there today. We don't know if it's a scheduled reset or a bug, so we've stopped trusting sandbox for anything beyond smoke tests.

title: **Transcript:** > **Interviewer:** Walk me through the last time you issued a ba
description:
**Transcript:**
> **Interviewer:** Walk me through the last time you issued a batch of virtual cards for a campaign.
>
> **Interviewee:** We had a BNPL promo, needed 2,000 cards live in under 10 minutes for a flash campaign tied to a marketing push. We hit rate limits almost immediately when we tried to push all 2,000 through at once.
>
> **Interviewer:** What did you do?
>
> **Interviewee:** We had to build our own internal queue that chunks requests into batches of 50 with a delay between each chunk. It works, but it's fragile — if the delay is too short we get throttled, too long and we miss the campaign window.
>
> **Interviewer:** How often does this come up?
>
> **Interviewee:** Every major campaign. At least once a month. It's become expected overhead in our planning now, which honestly shouldn't be normal.
>
> **Interviewer:** What would need to be true for this not to be a problem?
>
> **Interviewee:** An async batch endpoint. We submit the whole batch, get a job ID, and get notified when it's done. We don't need synchronous responses for 2,000 cards — we need reliability and a completion signal.

description: **Interviewee:** Product Manager, Fintech (persona: Chidinma Okoro's product counterpart)

title: **Transcript:** > **Interviewer:** Tell me about a time a customer complained ab
description:
**Transcript:**
> **Interviewer:** Tell me about a time a customer complained about their virtual card experience.
>
> **Interviewee:** Constantly, actually. Card gets created, and there's a lag before it's active. We don't get told when it flips to active — we just have to guess, or poll and hope we catch it soon after.
>
> **Interviewer:** What happens when you don't catch it in time?
>
> **Interviewee:** Customer calls support asking why the card isn't working. Half the time it actually is active by then, we just didn't know yet. So we're getting complaints about a problem that's already resolved on the backend — we just haven't heard about it.
>
> **Interviewer:** How does your team currently handle it?
>
> **Interviewee:** We poll every 30 seconds for the first five minutes after card creation. It's wasteful, and it still isn't fast enough to avoid the complaint volume.
>
> **Interviewer:** What would solve this?
>
> **Interviewee:** A webhook. Card status changes, you tell us immediately, we tell the customer immediately. That's it. It's not complicated on your end, I'd guess.

title: **Transcript:** > **Interviewer:** Walk me through what happens when a card gets
description:
**Transcript:**
> **Interviewer:** Walk me through what happens when a card gets blocked or frozen.
>
> **Interviewee:** Customer calls in reporting suspected fraud. We hit the freeze endpoint, get a 200 success response, dashboard shows "frozen." We tell the customer they're protected.
>
> **Interviewer:** And then?
>
> **Interviewee:** Sometimes a transaction still goes through in the next few minutes. We've had two disputes where the customer swears they saw a charge after we told them it was frozen — and they're right, it did happen, because the scheme hadn't caught up yet.
>
> **Interviewer:** How did that make your team feel?
>
> **Interviewee:** Exposed. We're telling customers something is true based on what your API tells us, and it turns out that's not always the real-time truth. That's a liability problem for us, not just an inconvenience.
>
> **Interviewer:** What would need to be true for this not to happen?
>
> **Interviewee:** I need confirmation that the freeze is actually live at the scheme level before I tell my dashboard — and my customer — that it's done.

title: **Interviewee:** Compliance Officer, Fintech (persona: Amara Nwachukwu)
description: **Interviewee:** Compliance Officer, Fintech (persona: Amara Nwachukwu)

title: **Transcript:** > **Interviewer:** Think of the most painful part of your curren
description:
**Transcript:**
> **Interviewer:** Think of the most painful part of your current workflow. Can you describe a specific moment when that pain showed up?
>
> **Interviewee:** Every CBN audit cycle. I need issuance and status logs for a specific date range. There's no self-serve way to get that — I open a support ticket and wait.
>
> **Interviewer:** How long does that usually take?
>
> **Interviewee:** Anywhere from two to five business days, depending on how backed up support is. If the audit deadline is tight, that's genuinely stressful.
>
> **Interviewer:** What do you do to work around it?
>
> **Interviewee:** I keep my own shadow spreadsheet, updated manually, so I'm not fully dependent on their turnaround. It's extra work I shouldn't have to do.
>
> **Interviewer:** What would need to be true for this not to be a problem?
>
> **Interviewee:** A dashboard where I filter by date range and export the log myself. I don't need anything fancy. I need independence from the ticket queue.

title: - **Hypothesis:** If we provide webhook notifications for card status changes, p
description:
- **Hypothesis:** If we provide webhook notifications for card status changes, participating fintechs will reduce polling-related support complaints by at least 40%.
- **Success Metric:** ≥40% reduction in "card not active" support tickets among beta participants within 30 days of enabling webhooks.
- **Failure Metric:** <15% reduction, or webhook delivery failure rate >2%.
- **Duration:** 6 weeks
- **Cost:** Medium — engineering time for webhook delivery infrastructure, retry logic, and beta monitoring
- **Risk:** Medium — delivery reliability at scale is unproven internally
- **Expected Learning:** Whether push-based status delivery meaningfully changes downstream support volume, and what delivery reliability threshold customers require to trust the mechanism.
- **Results:** Beta with 3 fintechs showed a 52% reduction in status-related tickets; webhook delivery failure rate held at 0.8%. Hypothesis supported — recommend general availability.
